subject: Regional data tethering & retention enclave Q&A
messages:
From: Jane Mendoza <jane.mendoza@aegisbank.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Cc: sec-requests@aegisbank.com
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions about snapshot/backups residency + deletion proof for private VPC

Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this. We're in procurement and security review for a private deployment of Redwood for several regulated lines of business. A few items we need clarified before the legal and controls review can advance:  

1) Residency of snapshots/backups: if we deploy Redwood Private in our AWS account, can you confirm all persistent snapshots, backups and any cold-tier copies are stored only in the same AWS region and account (no automatic cross-region replication) unless explicitly enabled by us?

2) Deletion proof: when we request a tenant-level wipe/sunset, what evidence does Redwood provide to show the data was removed from live stores, snapshot manifests, and from immutable/cold backups? We need an auditable certificate or logged artifact tied to the purge operation.

3) KMS / key ownership: do you offer customer-managed keys (CMK) such that Redwood cannot decrypt backups or snapshots? If yes, what key usage patterns do you require for restores/operations?

4) Legal hold / retention holds: if AegisBank places a legal hold, what is the mechanism to prevent automated lifecycle deletion while still allowing normal operations?

I've attached a quick spreadsheet with our baseline questions (Aegis-data-questions.xlsx). Can you point to the exact operational steps and SLAs? We're targeting an internal deadline the week of July 20.

Appreciate the help — happy to book a short call if that's easier.

Best,
Jane Mendoza
Senior Security Engineer, AegisBank
security@aegisbank.com

Jane — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (infrastructure) and Laura (account lead) so we can give both the operational and contractual answers. High-level answers below; we'll follow with a technical annex and a proposed MAP for AegisBank.

1) Residency: For Redwood Private deployed in a customer AWS account we default to storing object snapshots and local caches inside the same account and region by default. Cross-region replication is off by default and can only be turned on via an explicit config change by your ops team (or via a contract-scoped enable).

2) Deletion proof: We can produce an operator-signed deletion artifact that contains the snapshot manifest IDs, object hashes, and the list of storage locations that were purged. We'll propose a signed deletion certificate (PDF) and an entry in our audit trail that includes operator ID and job run ID.

3) KMS / CMK: We support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS CMKs). When CMKs are enabled, Redwood stores only ciphertext and cannot decrypt snapshots without you granting a temporary decrypt permission. We will document the exact IAM flow in the annex.

4) Legal hold: We support a legal/retention hold flag at the tenant level that prevents scheduled lifecycle jobs from removing objects. Holds are visible in the console and via the control-plane API. We'll outline the hold lifecycle and escalation steps in the annex.

Next steps: Karthik — can you prepare a short technical annex that covers 1) exact object locations for snapshots, 2) the deletion workflow (tombstone -> async purge -> manifest update), 3) the signed deletion artifact format, and 4) the CMK/IAM flow for restores? Laura — I'll follow up with a proposed MAP and SLA language (deletion timelines + attestation cadence).

Jane — happy to run a 30-minute deep-dive next week (I have availability July 12 and 15). Which works for you?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart

Subject: Re: Questions about snapshot/backups residency + deletion proof for private VPC (technical annex)

Jane / team — below is a concise technical summary; attaching a small diagram and a sample deletion-manifest for reference. Feel free to ping for details.

Operational model (Private deployment in your AWS account):
- Storage tenancy: persistent state (object store, KV cache) is in your AWS account/bucket namespacing by default. Redis-like caches are ephemeral on local instance storage.
- Replica policy: cross-region replication is disabled by default. We will not replicate outside your configured region without an explicit change from your admin role.
- Backups & cold-tier copies: snapshots are written as manifest + chunked objects into a region-local S3 bucket (or your equivalent object-store). Cold-tier retention (e.g., Glacier or equivalent) is opt-in.

Deletion workflow (customer-initiated tenant wipe / sunset):
1) Tombstone stage: objects and snapshot manifests are marked deleted in the control-plane metadata and a tombstone event is written to the audit log (audit id: RDW-AUD-<run-id>).
2) Async purge: object deletion jobs remove live object references; chunked objects are scheduled for garbage collection.
3) Manifest reconciliation: snapshot manifests are updated to reflect removed object digests.
4) Final scrub: once GC completes, an operator-signed deletion manifest is created with a list of object digests (SHA256) and storage keys that were removed.

Evidence & certificate:
- We can produce a signed deletion certificate (PDF) containing: tenant id, run id, operator id, timestamp, list of manifest ids, and SHA256 digest list for purged objects. The certificate will be PGP-signed by a Redwood operator key.

KMS & key control:
- CMK mode: customer-managed AWS KMS keys are supported. When enabled, ciphertext at rest remains unreadable to Redwood unless you grant decrypt permissions for a specific restore window. We log every use of the CMK decryption permission in the audit trail.
- Default mode: if you do not enable CMK, Redwood manages keys but we store only minimal metadata needed for orchestration; we do not retain customer plaintext in our operator consoles.

Legal hold / retention hold:
- A tenant-level retention flag blocks lifecycle deletion jobs and GC for objects under hold. Holds are surfaced in the control plane and in the deletion job pre-check step.
- Emergency unhold: requires a documented request and two-person approval from your SOC and our on-call (we record approvals in the audit trail).

Limitations & notes:
- Immutable backups created outside your account (e.g., if you opt in to cross-account snapshots) will require a separate removal path — we'll document and include that in the MAP.
- Cold-tier immutable archives (Glacier deep archive) will be subject to provider retention constraints; we recommend opt-out for immutable cold-tier unless required.

Attachments: kms_flow.svg (diagram of CMK flow), delete_manifest_example.txt (sample manifest with truncated SHA256 list).

Happy to walk through this on the call.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik and Evelyn — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our side before we finalize the security review:  

- SLA for deletion: we need a contractual SLA that defines 1) time-to-start (acknowledge + start purge job), 2) time-to-scrub (when objects are irrecoverable), and 3) certificate delivery (signed artifact). Can Redwood commit to timelines (we're looking for: start within 48 hours, final scrub within 72 hours) or propose alternatives?

- Deletion certificate: the PGP-signed manifest sounds good. We also want the certificate to include the operator audit id and a hash chain reference back to the audit log (so we can verify integrity).

- Legal hold process: request an explicit API endpoint to place/remove holds and the ability to export hold status as JSON for our compliance tooling. Also request a documented escalation path for emergency holds.

If you can provide a proposed MAP that includes the SLA language and an example deletion certificate, we can move the contract review forward. We're aiming for a pilot in August — dates hinge on this review.

Regards,
Jane

Subject: Re: Questions about snapshot/backups residency + deletion proof for private VPC — proposed MAP and SLAs

Jane — thanks. Per the thread we've pulled together a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and proposed SLA bullets below. Attaching a template deletion certificate and our proposed annex language for SLA inclusion.

Proposed MAP (high level):
- Week of Jul 12: technical deep-dive with Aegis infra and Redwood SREs (30 min) — confirm CMK/IAM flow and object naming conventions.
- Week of Jul 19: legal & procurement review of annex language (Redwood to provide annex draft).
- Aug 2: pilot tenant deploy in Aegis dev account (validate snapshot creation, manual wipe + deletion certificate issuance).
- Aug 9: pilot validation complete; produce first attestation report.

Proposed SLA bullets (to include in contract annex):
- Deletion start: Redwood will acknowledge and start tenant-level purge jobs within 48 hours of a validated request (business days).
- Final scrub: Redwood will complete asynchronous garbage collection and create an operator-signed deletion certificate within 7 calendar days; if CMK is in use and customer denies decrypt access, final scrub will be marked complete when object references are removed and manifest digests are produced (we'll note the CMK mode in the certificate).
- Certificate delivery: signed deletion certificate delivered via secure link and copied to the tenant audit log; certificate includes operator-id, RDW-AUD-<run-id>, timestamp, manifest ids and SHA256 digest list.
- Attestation cadence: quarterly attestation available on request; one-time deletion certificates issued per tenant wipe event.

Legal hold & tooling: we will expose tenant-level hold APIs (GET/POST/DELETE) and provide a JSON export of hold status and hold history for your compliance tooling. Emergency hold unfreeze requires documented request + two-party approval; we log all approvals.

Next actions: Laura will send the annex draft and the MAP as a shared Drive link. Karthik will prep the pilot checklist and I will prepare the deletion certificate template. If these items look good we can lock dates for the call on Jul 12 (Evelyn 10:00am-10:30am PT).

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Security & Compliance (Engage)
